snippet.title: Stop Building Fantasy Bug Out Bags | EP37
snippet.description:
Everybody talks about having a bug out bag, but most people never ask the real question: can you actually carry it, use it, and survive with it when things go bad?
In this episode of We Da People, Shelton, Colin, and Fred break down the real-world difference between a bug out bag, get home bag, vehicle survival kit, and everyday preparedness setup. This isn’t fantasy prepper talk. The crew gets into what should actually go in your bag, why your vehicle may be your first get home tool, and why your gear has to match your age, environment, family, training, and daily routine.
They also cover medical kits, water purification, rain gear, fire starting, tools, power banks, night vision, thermal, firearms, dry bags, and why training matters more than buying expensive survival gear. Fred brings a deeper preparedness mindset, Colin breaks down practical gear layers, and Shelton shares what he actually keeps in his bag and truck.
In this episode we cover:
- Bug out bag vs get home bag
- Why your vehicle matters in emergency preparedness
- How to organize a survival bag with modular kits
- Medical kit basics, trauma kits, Narcan, and tourniquets
- Water filters, Silcock keys, and water storage
- Fire starting tools, rain gear, boots, and dry bags
- Why bag weight can ruin your whole plan
- Training, field testing, and using the gear you carry

snippet.title: What Really Happens When the Power Grid Goes Down for MONTHS (Grid Down Survival Timeline)
snippet.description:
What Really Happens When the Power Grid Goes Down for MONTHS (Grid Down Survival Timeline)  




What would happen if the power grid failed for months instead of hours? This comprehensive grid-down survival scenario reveals the shocking reality of long-term blackouts that most people never consider. From cyber attacks and EMP threats to cascading infrastructure failures, our modern civilization hangs by a thread thinner than you think. In this detailed breakdown, we explore the three critical phases of societal collapse when the lights go out permanently - from the first 24 hours of denial to the brutal months-long struggle for survival that follows.

This isn't fear-mongering - it's reality-based preparedness education based on expert analysis and historical precedent. You'll discover the deadly mistakes that kill unprepared families in the first weeks, the essential skills that become more valuable than gold when technology fails, and the surprising ways human communities adapt and rebuild in the darkness. Whether you're new to prepping or an experienced survivalist, this grid-down timeline will change how you think about emergency preparedness and community resilience.

By understanding these vulnerabilities in our electrical infrastructure and learning from this comprehensive collapse scenario, you'll be better equipped to protect your family when disaster strikes. From water procurement and food preservation to community defense and psychological resilience, we cover every aspect of long-term grid-down survival. Don't wait until the lights go out to start preparing - your family's survival may depend on the decisions you make today.

snippet.title: 6 Days ALONE in the ALASKAN Wilderness | No FOOD, No Water!
snippet.description:
Join me for a week long solo wilderness survival challenge in the backcountry of South Central Alaska with no food or water. Watch me navigate the wilderness alone, find food, set up for tarp camping in a variety of weather conditions, and deal with hungry bears and other wildlife.

 By heading into an unfamiliar environment with nothing but my gear, I aim to demonstrate how to prioritize basic needs like water procurement and shelter building when you are completely on your own. This footage documents the raw reality of solo survival in extreme conditions.

Whether you are interested in wilderness survival strategies like off-grid food preservation or simply want to see how someone handles a high-stakes bushcraft challenge, this trip highlights the essential mindset required for solo wilderness survival. I break down the initial assessment of the terrain and how I plan to secure resources in a place I have never visited before. You will see firsthand how quickly the environment dictates your survival priorities and learn how to smoke salmon for storage when there's no refrigeration and may even pick up a few camping hacks or camping gear tips.

snippet.title: 5 Earthquakes in One Day… Is the Next BIG One Coming? Geophysicist Stefan Burns Explains
snippet.description:
In a single day, the ground ruptured across California, Japan, and Venezuela — including a rare and devastating "doublet" in Venezuela, where two major quakes struck just 39 seconds apart and the second was bigger than the first. Why is this happening? And what if some of it isn't entirely natural?

To make sense of it all, Neal K. Shah sits down with geophysicist Stefan Burns — a field scientist who has spent years recording earthquakes and mapping what's happening deep beneath our feet. Together they dig into the questions millions are asking: Can earthquakes be man-made? Could fracking, HAARP, or even the Sun be playing a role? Is Earth's weakening magnetic field making us more vulnerable? And most important for families — what actually keeps you and the people you love safe when the ground starts to shake?

Key Topics

Recent surge in global earthquakes
Potential natural and man-made triggers
Impact of solar activity and space weather
Earth's magnetic field and seismic risk
Earthquake safety tips and preparedness

Chapters

00:00 Introduction to Earthquake Phenomena
01:03 Understanding Recent Earthquake Clusters
03:54 Geopolitical Influences on Seismic Activity
06:47 Fracking and Its Connection to Earthquakes
09:36 The Role of HAARP and Ionospheric Effects
12:46 Solar Activity and Its Impact on Earthquakes
20:38 The Weakening Magnetic Field and Its Implications
25:55 Practical Advice During Earthquakes
29:43 The Scary Potential of Solar Events

IN THIS EPISODE

* The 2026 Venezuela earthquake doublet — M7.2 and M7.5 only 39 seconds apart, and why doublets are so rare and so deadly
* Why a M5.6 near the San Andreas, in a spot with no recorded quake that size in 200+ years, may be a signal worth watching
* "Man-made earthquakes": what fracking and induced seismicity genuinely can — and can't — cause
* HAARP and ionospheric heaters — what the science says they actually do, and where speculation begins
* The proposed Sun–Earth connection: solar wind, solar flares, coronal holes, geomagnetic storms, and the theory linking them to major quakes
* Earth's weakening magnetic field, the South Atlantic Anomaly, and the pole-reversal debate
* Practical earthquake safety: P-waves, early-warning seconds, and the run-outside vs. stay-put debate
* The Carrington Event and Miyake events — the solar superstorms that could set modern civilization back

ABOUT OUR GUEST — STEFAN BURNS
Stefan posts near-daily geophysics updates on the Sun, the Earth, and seismic activity.
YouTube: @StefanBurns
X: @StefanBurnsGeo
Website: earthevolution.com

ABOUT THIS CHANNEL
Neal K. Shah is a Johns Hopkins- and NIH-funded caregiving researcher covering the topics that matter most to older adults and the families who care for them. Subscribe for clear, careful conversations on health, science, and protecting the people you love.

If you know someone in an earthquake zone, share this video and help them make a plan.

Some theories discussed are emerging or debated within the scientific community and are presented to explore open questions, not as settled conclusions. For earthquake preparedness, always follow official guidance from the USGS and your local emergency authorities.

snippet.title: What Really Happens to Your Stuff After an EMP — and the 5 Things That Still Work
snippet.description:
📘 My complete survival manual — 150+ cheap-first methods: https://collapse-proof-home-manual.ne...

Everything I teach on this channel, in one place — how to keep your family warm, fed, watered, powered, and safe when the grid, the trucks, or the dollar stop. 250+ pages, 13 systems, ~50 plain illustrations — every number sourced, every price honest, cheap-first, and calm. No bunker, no doomsday, no fear. You're not paranoid — you're early.

-------- You've seen the movie version of an EMP: one flash in the sky and every car dies, the lights go out forever, and it's the apocalypse by Tuesday. The actual evidence says something very different — and much more useful. In this video I separate the real from the hype, using documented sources, and then give you the five kinds of things that genuinely keep working when the grid goes down.

The best news comes at the end: almost every one of those five things is exactly what you'd want in an ordinary week-long blackout — so you cannot waste your money, and you do not need expensive "EMP-proof" gear.

In this video:

What an EMP actually is — the man-made kind and the sun's version
What the U.S. government's own EMP Commission found when it tested cars (hint: most kept running)
The far more likely event nobody talks about: a geomagnetic storm (Quebec went dark for 9 hours in 1989)
The 5 kinds of things that survive: simple/unplugged tools, older engines, a $20 Faraday can, disconnected solar, and paper
The Faraday-cage myths — you don't need to bury it or ground it
Why a piece of paper is the most EMP-proof technology on Earth

Sources referenced: the U.S. EMP Commission vehicle testing (37 cars; only 3 stalled at the highest field levels; about 1 in 10 showed serious effects); Starfish Prime, the 1962 high-altitude test that knocked out streetlights in Hawaii; the March 1989 geomagnetic storm that blacked out Hydro-Québec for about nine hours; the 1859 Carrington Event; and NASA's account of the July 2012 solar storm near-miss.

Cole Merritt is a composite educational character presented with an AI-generated voice and avatar. This channel provides general preparedness education — not professional advice, and not a prediction about any specific event. For your own situation, check with your local emergency management and qualified professionals.

snippet.description:
Join Brother Wood as he crafts three distinct bushcraft shelters deep in the wilderness, using only natural materials found in the forest. snippet.title: 10 Steps to Take When the Grid Goes Down and You Don't Know for How Long | Real Blackout Playbook
snippet.description:
Step one: Fill everything. Tub, pots, buckets, bottles. You have maybe 45 minutes of water pressure left. That's the cleanest water you'll see for a while.

Step two: Confirm the scope. Your house, your block, or your whole region? Battery radio or car radio tells you what you're dealing with. Starlink Mini gives you full details if you have it.

Step three: Send one text to family with your status. Then put the phone in low power mode. Cell towers may not last long.

Step four: Fridge and freezer stay shut. Snap a photo of both interiors so you don't have to guess. Eat in order: fridge first, freezer second, pantry last.

Step five: Stay out of stores. Whatever's in your pantry is the plan. If this is a big event, everyone else is about to panic. Avoid crowds.

Step six: Shrink your living space. One small room, blankets over windows and doorways. Critical in winter, similar approach for extreme heat.

Step seven: Combustion stays outside. Generators, grills, camp stoves. Carbon monoxide kills more people in blackouts than anything else. This one is life or death.

Step eight: Run dark and quiet. Don't be the brightest, loudest house on the street. That makes you the most interesting house. Generator during the day, blackout curtains at night.

Step nine: Get comms up. Cell towers may fail within a day or two. Battery radio for info in, GMRS for local family communication out.

Step ten: In a big blackout, nobody is coming to help you. Plan accordingly.

A few things worth knowing:

Blackouts historically last hours to a few days, but the 2003 Northeast blackout affected 55 million people and the 2021 Texas grid failure killed over 200 people. Big events do happen. And likely will happen with more frequency. 

A whole house generator is great, but a small portable generator with 3 to 5 gallons of stabilized fuel plus a portable power station covers most scenarios and doesn't announce itself to the whole neighborhood.

Water heaters hold 40 to 80 gallons of usable water. Learn how to drain yours from the bottom valve. That's a free reservoir most people forget.

Practice this before you need it. A weekend without power at home tells you exactly where your gaps are.

snippet.title: OFF GRID AND BULLET PROOF! PREPARING FOR AN EMP OR FOR THE GRID TO GO DOWN. HOMESTEAD UPDATE
snippet.description:
I want to build a faraday cage inside of a metal shipping container. I will need to keep the cage inside insulated from the ground but the metal shell really gets me started!

You never really know when the lights are going to go out! One solar flare, one high-altitude weapon, one cyber attack, and the grid could drop in seconds. That’s the reality of an EMP (Electromagnetic Pulse)! It's a massive burst of electromagnetic energy capable of frying electronics, disabling vehicles, knocking out communications, and throwing modern life back a hundred years in an instant.

In this video, I show you how I’m turning a shipping container into a secure, multipurpose storage unit to protect sensitive electronics and critical gear, not just from weather, thieves, and bullets... but from the invisible threat of an EMP.

What’s inside my off-grid prep setup? Why a steel shipping container can act like a giant Faraday cage? How to use containers for food storage, workshops, bunkers, or even tiny homes? And why preparing before the grid goes down is the only real insurance policy you’ll ever have!

Whether you’re into off-grid living, prepping, homesteading, or just being self-reliant, this build might give you a few new ideas for securing what matters most when the world goes dark.
